Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS 1 2578 ^1978 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
SQUASH RACKET FRAMES 

(First Revision) 

0. FOREWORD 

©•1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian 
Standards Institution on 27 November 1978, after the draft finalized by 
the Sports Goods Sectbnal Committee had been approved by the 
Consumer Products and Medical Instruments Division Council. 

0*2 This standard was 5rst published in 1963 and is being revised to 
incorporate the suggestions received from time to time. 

0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, express- 
ing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*, 
The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should 
be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard covers the requirements for two grades of squash racket 
frames designated as * Grade 1 ' and ' Grade 2 '• 

2. GRADES 

2.1 Squash racket frames shall be classified into two grades, namely, 
Grade 1 and Grade 2 according to the following requirements. 

2*1.1 Gfiuf^l— The frame shall be of five to seven-ply laminated 
construction with reinforced shoulders minimum 3 ash ply. 

2«1«2 Gradi 2-^ The frame shall be of five to seven-ply laminated cons- 
truction with reinforced shoulders. 



* Rules for rounding off numerical values ( reviud), 

3 



IS 1 2578 .1978 

3. MATERIAL 

3.1 The timber shall be straight-graincd and free from knots, cracks, open 
splits, decay and stain. It shall be well-seasoned with moisture content 
within the range of 9 to 12 percent ( see IS : 287-1973* ). 

3.1.1 Bend — The bend shall be laminated with two-ply each of ash 
( Fraxinus sp ) and beech ( Fagus sp ) for Grade 1 of frame, and with 
minimum three-ply of ash ( Fraxinus sp ) and beech ( Fagus sp ) for Grade 2 
of frame; and any one of the following combinations of timbers: 

a) beech ( Fagus sp ) and birch ( Betula sp ), 

b) walnut ( Juglans sp ) and fibre, 

c) hickory ( Caroa sp ), and 

d) maple ( Acer sp). 

3.1.2 Handle 

3.1.2.1 For Grade 1 the handle shall be made from suitably chamfered 
willow ( Salix alba var Coerulea ), lime ( Citrus sp ) or toon ( Cedrela toona 
Roxb. ). 

3.1.2.2 For Grade 2 the handle shall be made from toon ( Cedrela toona 
Roxb. ) or poplar ( Fopulus sp), suitably chamfered. 

3.1.3 Wedge 

3.1.3.1 For Grade 1 the wedge shall be made of ash ( Fraxinus sp), 
beech ( Fagus sp ) or sycamore ( Acer Fseudo Platanus ). 

3.1.3.2 For Grade 2 the wedge shall be made of ash ( Fraxinus sp ) or 
beech {Fagus sp). 

3.2 Grip — The grip shall be made of leather, leather cloth, or towel, as 
may be specified by the purchaser. 

4. CONSTRUCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS 

4.1 All plies shall be properly glued with synthetic resin adhesive {see 
IS : 851-19571 ) and securely fitted to make a proper bend. 

4.2 Wedges shall be glued and adjusted at the throat of the bends. 

4.3 The pieces of the handle shall be properly glued and strongly pressed. 

4.4 The shoulders shall be reinforced with U-shapcd face-plates by the 
help of glue, the veneer being of ash, beech or brimji ( Celtis australis 
Linn. )• 



* Recommendations for maximum permissible moisture content of timber used for 
different purposes. 

tSpecification for synthetic resin adhesives for construction work in wood. 



IS 1 2578 -1978 

4.5 The surfaces of the bend and throat shall be smoothly rounded or 
bevelled. The edges of the holes on the bend for the gut shall be smoothly 
rounded off. 

4.6 The frames shall be finely sand-papered, polished with cellulose 
lacquer and trimmed attractively. 

4.7 The handle shall be either rounded or semi-roundcd and covered with 
grooved grips of leather, leather cloth, rubber or towel. 

4.8 The dimensions of the frame shall be as indicated in Fig. 1. 

4.9 Holes — The number of holes shall be 54 to 56. The diameter of 
each hole shall be 2'0 ± 0*2 mm. 

5. SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 

5.1 The sampling scheme and criteria for acceptance for squash racket 
frames shall be agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. A suitable 
sampling scheme and criteria for acceptance are given in Appendix A. 

6. DESIGNATION 

6#1 The designation of a squash racket shall indicate: 

a) grade, and 

b) IS number. 

Examplei 

Grade 1 of squash racket shall be designated as: 
Squash racket, Grade I, IS : 2578 

7. MARKING AND PACKING 

7.1 Unless otherwise required by the purchaser, each squash racket shall be 
marked on the throat and handle of the frame with the manufacturer's or 
supplier's initials or trade-mark. 

7,1.1 The squash racket frames may also be marked with the ISI 
Certification Mark. 

Note — The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the 
Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations 
made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard 
conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements 
of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and qiulity control 
which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. ISI marked 
producu are also contmuously checked by ISI for conformity to that stamlard as a 
^rther safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the ISI 
Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obuined 
ftom the Indian Standards Institution.

7»2 Rackets shall be packed in weather-proof material in accordance with 
the best prevalent trade practice.

tured by the same firm shall be grouped together to constitute a lot.

A.2. INSPECTION AND CRITERIA FOR ACCEPTANCE 

A-2.1 Each racket in the test samples shall fint be examined for materials 
used in the construction as given in 3. If any racket in the test samples 
is noticed to have been made up of materials other than those specified^ bXL 
the rackets in the lot shall be examined and those non«conforming shall be 
rejected. 



IS 1 2578 -1978 

A-2J.1 All the rackets in the lot which conform to the requirements of 
material shall constitute a fresh lot which shall be sampled afresh in 
accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 1 for the purpose of testing in A«2*2. 

A-2.2 If the rackets are made up of the specified materials, then each 
racket of the test samples shall be tested for the dimensional and construc- 
tional requirements as given under 4. 

A*2.3 During testing as in A-2*2, the sample racket failing to satisfy any 
one or more of the requirements of 4.1 to 4,9 shall be deemed as defective. 

A-2.4 The lot shall be declared as conforming to this standard if the 
number of defective rackets in the sample does not exceed the number 
given in col 3 of Table 1.
